Hey friends! I had an idea. Inspired by many of your comments about putting my videos on in the background (to cook... clean... or even to fall asleep to), I decided to create something just for you.

This is a Murder, Mystery & Makeup Compilation... over 3 hours long... featuring a few cold cases and stories that left me with a whole lot of unanswered questions. Like, these are the ones I think about all the time. Because there's still so many details that don't add up.

Sweet dreams! lol

comments.text: When has anyone ever heard of a police department declaring someone dead on the spot and sending them straight to the morgue without medical personnel present or any attempt at resuscitation? That in itself is suspicious. Standard procedure typically involves paramedics assessing the individual, officially pronouncing death if necessary, and only then does the body get transferred—often with an ambulance involved, not a police-issued transport to the morgue. For law enforcement to bypass medical professionals raises red flags: Were proper protocols ignored? Was there pressure to close a case quickly? This kind of deviation from protocol not only undermines public trust but also invites questions about transparency, accountability, and the possibility of a cover-up. In high-profile or controversial cases, such actions can fuel rumors and erode confidence in the system entirely.

Ohhhh. I thought mine made sense, but Bailey's covers everything.

The farm one. I grew up in a rural area. We had volunteer fire and rescue. In major emergencies, we had no choice but to grab someone and just run because it took so long for rescue to arrive. So we would have to grab the person. At the time, we didnt have cell phones. In some cases people would drive to the fire and rescue building to get them to the ambulance. Many times farmers would dial 911, tell them what happened, give the vehicle they were driving and if they were heading to the rescue station or into town directly to the hospital. This saved many lives. Unfortunately  we did have a few rollovers in back fields and again it being before cell phones, they were not found for hours and passed away.
